title: Haircut Numbers Explained: Clipper Guard Sizes from 0 to 8
hero_alt: Numbered clipper guards lined up in their case
image_plan: ai: flat-lay of numbered barber clipper guard combs on black, black and white, no people
card_text: What a 1, a 3 or an 8 actually leaves on your head, in inches, plus why a fade is never just one number.
lede: Haircut numbers are clipper guard sizes, and each number stands for how much hair the guard leaves behind. On the standard scale, a 1 leaves about 1/8 inch, a 2 about 1/4 inch, a 3 about 3/8 inch and a 4 about 1/2 inch, climbing by roughly 1/8 inch per number up to an 8, which leaves about an inch. A 0 means no guard at all, just the bare blade.
Below is the full chart, what each length looks like on a head, and how to use the numbers to ask for exactly the cut you want.

seo.title: Clipper Guard Sizes 0 to 8, Explained | Carlsbad, NM
seo.description: Haircut numbers explained by a Carlsbad, NM barber: what each clipper guard from 0 to 8 leaves on your head, and how to ask for a 1 on the sides.

blocks.heading: Guard numbers, in inches.
blocks.lead: Standard sizes. Sets from different makers can vary slightly.
rows: 1/32 to 1/16 in, set by the lever

blocks.heading: What each range looks like.
blocks.lead: Numbers are easier to picture in groups.

subsections.heading: 0 to 1
paragraphs: Scalp shows through clearly. This is the range for the shortest part of a fade, a very close buzz, or the sides under a longer top. Lighter hair over lighter skin looks barer here than dark, dense hair does.

subsections.heading: 2 to 3
paragraphs: Short, but you can see hair color and some texture. A 2 or 3 all over is the classic buzz cut length people picture, and it's a common choice for the sides of a taper.

subsections.heading: 4 to 5
paragraphs: Enough length to cover the scalp evenly. Hair starts to show its direction and grain. Many short crops sit in this range on top.

subsections.heading: 6 to 8
paragraphs: The long end of clipper work. At an 8 you have about an inch, and past that most tops are cut with scissors so they can be shaped instead of kept one even length.

blocks.heading: A fade isn't one number.
paragraphs: A fade moves through several lengths from the bottom up. It might start at bare skin, pass through a 1 and a 2, and finish blended into a 4 on top. The skill is in hiding where one length ends and the next begins, which is done by working the lever and the blade between guard sizes, not just swapping combs.

That's why "a 1 fade" can mean different things to different people. To one person it means a 1 at the very bottom; to another it means the whole side cut to a 1. Saying where you want it short, and how short, clears that up.
When the bottom goes past a 0 to bare skin, that's a skin fade. The finish there is done closer than any guard can go.

blocks.heading: Use the numbers well.
paragraphs: If you know your numbers, use them like this: "a 1 on the sides, blended into a 3 on top." That tells me the shortest point, the longest point and roughly how much blending sits between them.

If you don't know your numbers, that's normal. A photo works just as well, and a picture of your last cut on a day you liked it works even better. Either way, the cut is booked as a regular haircut on Booksy.

Hair type changes how a number reads, too. Curly and coily hair springs back after it's cut, so a 3 can look shorter on curls than on straight hair. Thick, dark hair looks fuller at the same number than fine, light hair does.

items.q: What number is a buzz cut?
items.a: Any single guard all over. Shorter buzzes sit around a 1 or 2; longer ones around a 3 or 4.

items.q: Is a 0 the same as bald?
items.a: No. A 0 is the bare clipper blade, which still leaves a fine layer. Bald or skin takes a closer tool.

items.q: Does a higher number mean longer hair?
items.a: Yes. Each step up the scale leaves about 1/8 inch more.
